claim: A send command that waits for delivery confirmation costs orchestrators about a quarter of their working time.

metric.what: Wall time of each foreground send tool call (call to result) in orchestrator transcripts, against total orchestrator in-turn time.

countedFrom.machine: one Windows 11 machine; one master, 8 orchestrators, about 50 short-lived workers, one person
versions: agent harness as installed in the period (exact version not recorded)

proposedChange: The send command returns once the message is durably queued; delivery failure is reported to the sender as a message. Until then, the protocol tells every orchestrator to run sends in the background.
whyItGeneralises: Any fleet whose coordinators send by a command that blocks until delivery pays the same tax; the share scales with how many messages a coordinator sends per turn, not with this machine.
limits: One orchestrator's sends were not recognised by the command pattern and are excluded. The lowest share belongs to the one orchestrator that already backgrounds its sends.
